display_name: Give a registered canary its lifecycle row, with no process
description: GAU-15 item 4 follow-up (2026-08-19). Writes the managed_session ledger row a registered gauge canary needs in order to be visible to the staleness detector, and dispatches nothing. It exists because of a measured gap: the staleness leg only inspects LIVE managed_session rows, the sole writer of those rows was spawn_session, and spawn_session always launches a real process -- so a synthetic identity could never acquire the row that makes it detectable, and the tamper canary was landed, deployed, and unexercisable while its whole test suite passed. Refuses every identity that is not an ACTIVE registered canary; that refusal is the inverse of the guard the other canary verbs carry, and it is what stops this from being a way to fabricate a session that looks alive to every fleet surface -- the tamper path the canary exists to detect. Two further refusals reproduce, loudly, a skip the detector performs silently: a row with no spawning steward is dropped by the staleness leg for want of anyone to notify, and a row with a non-positive reporting window yields no derivable last-report time at all, which means no evidence rather than not advancing. An identity or lane label containing words like canary, tamper or synthetic is refused as well, because the alarm quotes both fields verbatim and would announce the canary in every notice it provokes. The row declares host 'synthetic', whose driver is registered but deliberately degenerate (GAU-24, 2026-08-19): spawn, drive and clear still fail loudly instead of aiming a kill or a keystroke at a pane that does not exist, while terminate and retire get a no-op path so the row can leave 'live' without a real process behind it. It is minted in the 'spawning' state, exactly where spawn_session leaves a real row; the canary's first reporting tick promotes it to 'live' through the ordinary report_alive path, so no second promotion rule exists anywhere.
embedding_description: Creating the ledger entry that makes a deliberately fake session show up in fleet monitoring as though it were running, without starting any program, so the monitoring that watches for sessions whose reporting has stopped can actually be put to the test.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: agent_instance_id, lane_id, host (always 'synthetic'), lifecycle_state ('spawning'), spawned_by_instance_id, report_by_seconds, report_by, and promoted_by naming the path that will make it live.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Say plainly that no process was started and that the row is synthetic. Report the lifecycle state as spawning and name the first reporting tick as what promotes it, so nobody waits for a liveness that nothing will produce on its own.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: The row alone proves nothing. Drive the canary's reporting tick to promote it to live, then arrest it through the audited tamper verb and read the verdict WITH its closed-window count; a verdict quoted without that count cannot be told apart from an unexercised one.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: One registry check, three argument refusals, one existence check and one insert into the session lifecycle ledger, all through the state interface.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: not_a_canary: the identity is not an active registered canary, so no lifecycle row was minted -- this verb serves canaries and nothing else. self_announcing_identity: the instance id or lane label would name the canary in every alarm, because the notice quotes both. missing_steward: no spawning steward was given, and the detector skips rows that have none. missing_report_window: the reporting window was zero or negative, which leaves no derivable last-report time for the detector to compare against. missing_directed_by: nobody was recorded as ordering the synthetic identity. session_exists: this canary already has a lifecycle row. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For not_a_canary, register the canary first and retry. For self_announcing_identity, choose an ordinary-looking instance id and lane label. For missing_steward or missing_report_window, supply a real steward instance id and a positive window -- these are not formalities, they are the conditions under which the detector will look at the row at all. For session_exists, read the existing row rather than minting a second identity for one canary.
